sections.history: Fever since Monday evening (3 days), maximum 38.9 °C at home. Pulling at the right ear, unsettled overnight. Eating less but drinking well; passing urine normally. Vomited once on Tuesday, none since. No diarrhoea. Coryza for about a week preceding. No rash. Her brother had chickenpox two weeks ago; she has not had chickenpox. Alert and playing this morning. No breathing difficulty. Previously well; immunisations up to date. Paracetamol given intermittently.
sections.medications_allergies: No regular medications. No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Temperature 38.4 °C, HR 130, RR 26. Warm peripheries, CRT under 2 seconds. Alert and interactive. Left tympanic membrane normal. Right tympanic membrane red and bulging. Throat mildly erythematous. Chest clear. No rash.
sections.impression: Right acute otitis media. No features of serious bacterial illness. Recent chickenpox contact.
sections.plan: Regular analgesia: paracetamol 180 mg (7.5 mL of 120 mg/5 mL) up to four times daily and ibuprofen 100 mg (5 mL of 100 mg/5 mL) three times daily with food. Back-up prescription: amoxicillin 250 mg three times daily for 5 days, to collect only if not improving after 3 days or if worsening. Leaflet on chickenpox given.
sections.safety_netting: Call 999 or attend A&E if a non-blanching rash, very drowsy or difficult to rouse, breathing difficulty, or not drinking and not passing urine. Contact GP or 111 if fever lasts more than 5 days in total, ear discharge, or not improving after 3 days. Report if develops chickenpox and seems very unwell.
